cases.name: In re Delhi Laws Act, 1912
cases.facts: The Court examined statutory provisions delegating legislative power to the executive.
cases.issue: What legislative functions may constitutionally be delegated?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The legislature may delegate ancillary functions but cannot abdicate its essential legislative policy-making function.
cases.holding: The Court laid down the foundational excessive-delegation principle.
cases.relevance: Use as the leading Indian authority on permissible delegation.

cases.name: Hamdard Dawakhana (Wakf) Lal Kuan, Delhi v. Union of India
cases.facts: A statutory provision conferred power to add matters to a prohibited category without adequate legislative guidance.
cases.issue: Whether unguided executive power amounted to excessive delegation.
cases.ratioDecidendi: A delegation lacking adequate legislative policy or guidance is impermissible.
cases.relevance: Use for the requirement of policy, standards and guidance in delegated legislation.

cases.name: Gwalior Rayon Silk Mfg. (Wvg.) Co. Ltd. v. Assistant Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court considered the extent to which legislative functions could be delegated.
cases.issue: What distinguishes permissible delegation from abdication of legislative responsibility?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The legislature must retain essential legislative functions while permitting subordinate legislation to fill in details within the policy laid down.
cases.holding: The Court applied the distinction between essential legislative function and implementation detail.

learningObjectives: Explain the constitutional and statutory basis of delegated legislation.
Apply the excessive-delegation and parent-statute consistency tests.
Distinguish permissible delegation of detail from abdication of essential legislative function.
Analyse procedural and substantive grounds for judicial review of subordinate legislation.
enhancement.definition: Delegated legislation is subordinate law made under authority conferred by a parent enactment. Its validity depends on the parent Act, the constitutional distribution of legislative power, the limits of the delegation and compliance with mandatory rule-making requirements.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The legislature may delegate implementation and ancillary detail but cannot surrender an essential legislative function. A rule, notification or bye-law must remain within the parent Act and cannot contradict its text, purpose or mandatory limits.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India; the specific parent Act and its rule-making provision; applicable laying, publication, consultation or approval requirements.
essentialIngredients: Identify the parent Act and precise rule-making provision.
Identify the policy or legislative standard supplied by the parent legislature.
Test the subordinate instrument against the parent Act and Constitution.
Check mandatory procedural conditions for making the instrument.
Separate permissible implementation detail from excessive delegation or contradiction of the parent law.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The excessive-delegation inquiry asks whether the legislature has retained the essential legislative function while entrusting administration with subordinate rule-making. The parent statute must supply the policy and standards required by constitutional doctrine. Judicial review also tests whether the subordinate instrument stays within the four corners of the parent Act and whether mandatory procedures for making it were followed. The fact that a rule is convenient or administratively useful cannot cure a conflict with the parent statute.
examples: A rule fills in forms, time limits or technical details expressly contemplated by the parent Act; that is ordinarily implementation rather than excessive delegation.
A rule adds a substantive prohibition or liability that the parent Act does not authorise; the issue is whether the rule enlarges the statute and is ultra vires.
A parent Act requires prior consultation or laying and the prescribed step is omitted; the legal consequence depends on whether the requirement is mandatory in the statutory scheme.
A delegation leaves no intelligible legislative policy or standard while transferring the essential choice to the executive; the excessive-delegation doctrine is engaged.
enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the parent provision; state the legislative policy; compare the impugned rule with the parent Act; test constitutional and procedural limits; then formulate the precise declaration or quashing relief.
keyTakeaways: Delegated legislation derives validity from the parent statute.
Essential legislative policy cannot simply be abdicated to the executive.
A subordinate instrument cannot enlarge or contradict the parent Act.
Judicial review of subordinate legislation is legality review, not a general policy appeal.
